But this routine still cannot get an IBKR-confirmed answer, and every automated price source (Yahoo query1/query2, stooq, CNN, Google Finance, WSJ, MarketWatch) returned network-egress errors again today — a full outage, not a single-ticker gap.

One watch item for later: Alphabet's 2026 capex budget (up to $205B) alongside a reported negative quarterly free cash flow of $5.9B — worth revisiting if sentiment on AI capex turns, but not an action item today.

No fresh discovery candidate generated automatically here by design — that's stock-finder. Your call.

📚 Today you learned

Price Feed Redundancy — Why "No Price" Beats "Wrong Price"

Every automated price source this routine relies on — Yahoo's two endpoints, Stooq, CNN, Google Finance, WSJ, MarketWatch — failed the same way today: blocked at the network layer, not a bad ticker or a holiday. That's a correlated failure, not six independent ones, because they all sit behind the same egress path in this environment. The discipline that matters isn't finding a seventh source to paper over the gap — it's refusing to guess. GOOG's stop is either intact or it isn't; a search snippet saying "+3.0% Monday" is directional color, not a number to act on. This is exactly why your IBKR stop brackets don't depend on this email running at all — the broker enforces them independently of whether Claude can fetch a quote. The email's job is monitoring and judgment; the broker's bracket order is the actual safety net.

Also today: Correlated failure — when multiple "independent" systems share a hidden common dependency (here: one network path), they fail together instead of covering for each other.
